doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Day job as a clerk and time with his children in the Bronx
summary: For nine years he worked office jobs by day, and spent time with his children, living in the Bronx.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, in 1952 you’re working in New York. Were you able to support your family at that time as a singer?

I had to take other outside work in the day. I had a day job for nine years. I was various kinds of a clerk. I worked in offices. I worked in all different kinds of offices, usually typing invoices. I was part of New York’s office pool of workers. I hated the conversations that the people had in those offices. One of the questions that drove me mad was, “Did you watch the Lucy show last night?” I told the office manager one time, “Not only did I not watch the Lucy show last night, but I have never watched the Lucy show.” She says, “What’s the matter with him?” She got so mad at me. She was – she didn’t speak to me for two days.
I believe that. How did you manage your time during that period? How did you balance your time between your job, your music, and your family?

When I was working, like on the nights when I had a job, I would come straight home from work and take my children out and make sure that they had a little time with me. I would take them on long walks. We’d walk all around the neighborhood. Anything that they wanted to show me, I was glad to see, and I would talk to them. We’d sit on the bench, and we’d talk. I’d buy them lollypops and ice cream and all that stuff. I tried to spend as much time with them as I could, because I knew later on, when they went to sleep, I was going to go to work, and I wasn’t going to be able to get up with them in the morning, because I had to go to work. So I tried to spend as much time as possible with them.
What part of New York were you living in then?
I lived in the Bronx: 201st Street and Gun Hill Road, just this side of White Plains, before it became Fort Apache. It was quite a nice place to live in those days. It was the Bronx, still.
That makes sense. Jerry Gonzalez and Fort Apache- he was from that area.
It’s what Damon Runyan called the Bronix.
